name: Mass Babify stuns, transforms, regenerates and breaks on damage (#1349)
contract: Mass Babify 520855 needs no script: effect 0 is aura 12 SPELL_AURA_MOD_STUN with Mechanic 17 (AuraEffect::HandleAuraModStun, the 'preventing them from acting' half), effect 1 is aura 56 SPELL_AURA_TRANSFORM with EffectMiscValue 26365 (AuraEffect::HandleAuraTransform, the baby), and effect 2 is aura 23 SPELL_AURA_PERIODIC_TRIGGER_SPELL at EffectAmplitude 1000 firing Babify 801260, a SPELL_EFFECT_HEAL_PCT with EffectBasePoints 2 (die 1 => 3%) handled by Spell::EffectHealPct - the 'rapidly regenerate health' half, 30000 per second against a 1000000 maximum. 'Damage dealt will interrupt this effect' is AuraInterruptFlags 524290, whose 0x2 bit is the native take-damage interrupt. DurationIndex 64 = 40000 ms, matching the tooltip's 40 seconds. The fixture creature is a critter template (Dig Rat 3444, creature_template.type 8): AscensionCompat's CanScaleCreature (AscensionCompat.cpp:6093-6099) excludes critters from local level scaling, so it keeps the maximum health CoAGameplayTest asked for instead of having it rebuilt by Creature::SelectLevel, and it still has room to take a melee swing at the end after four seconds of regeneration. The scenario asserts no maximum of its own: the regeneration clause is 3% of maximum health per second, so it is read as a percentage with health_pct, which is what the tooltip states and is independent of whatever the maximum turns out to be. The dummy is dropped to one hit point rather than to a fixed fraction for the same reason - one is a valid health fixture for any maximum.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Drop the dummy low enough that four seconds of regeneration are visible
Mass Babify lands on the nearby enemy
Let at least one Babify tick land
The babified enemy regenerates 3% of maximum health per second
